answer: Policies are written in zenith, settled in anchor, and pearl lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 24% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 291 aliases cost 106 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
